steps.name: Ezell
steps.text: Cecelia, watch out!

steps.name: Cecelia
steps.text: Mister Ezell!

steps.name: Patia
steps.text: Guide... We have to hold our ground!

steps.name: Ezell
steps.text: It's you! Cecelia isn't your bargaining chip!

steps.name: Fiammetta
steps.text: Ezell, give her to me!

steps.name: Fiammetta
steps.text: Hey, Ezell! What's the big idea? Don't tell me you're working with these...

steps.name: Patia
steps.text: Heretics? Terrorists? Apostates? Are those the only names that the Church can come up with?

steps.name: Fiammetta
steps.text: Out of the way, Patia!

steps.name: Patia
steps.text: You were right, Fiammetta... It's not easy to change the way someone thinks.

steps.name: Patia
steps.text: That goes for both of us.

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: You look like you're doing well.

steps.name: Mostima
steps.text: Much thanks to you. You look like you've aged a lot, though... 'Guide.'

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: Haha, I have you to thank for that, too. The gunshot wound took forever to heal.

steps.name: Mostima
steps.text: Hahaha, not bad. Definitely better than having her shoot you.

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: That is true.

steps.name: Mostima
steps.text: Lemuen almost died.

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: I know.

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: It was the better option, over her bullet.

steps.name: Mostima
steps.text: Looks like that mental illness of yours hasn't gotten any better.

steps.name: Mostima
steps.text: Hey, kid. You must be Ezell.

steps.name: Ezell
steps.text: (Another Legata...? What should I...?)

steps.name: Ezell
steps.text: A fallen angel?! Miss Fiammetta, what's going on?

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: Ah... you fell. Of course. You shot at me.

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: You can't feel anymore.

steps.name: Mostima
steps.text: So I use my eyes to see and my mind to think.

steps.name: Mostima
steps.text: The little girl there is Cecelia, right?

steps.name: Cecelia
steps.text: Miss, you have horns, but you also have a halo... Are you a Sankta?

steps.name: Mostima
steps.text: Uh, maybe? I don't exactly know, actually.

steps.name: Mostima
steps.text: Listen, Ezell. Bring Cecelia over here. She'll be fine.

steps.name: Ezell
steps.text: I'm supposed to trust a fallen angel?

steps.name: Mostima
steps.text: I've gotta be more trustworthy than a pissed-off Liberi.

steps.name: Fiammetta
steps.text: Hey! You mean that bitch over there, right?!

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: Mostima... We haven't finished her mother's funeral yet.

steps.name: Mostima
steps.text: Whoa, I almost bought into that. Are you really such a dutiful curate for this Ecclesia Requietum, Andoain?

steps.name: Fiammetta
steps.text: Mostima! Did you follow me here just to catch up on old times?

steps.name: Mostima
steps.text: Ezell, have you made up your mind yet?

steps.name: Ezell
steps.text: Cecelia, we...

steps.name: Cecelia
steps.text: Miss...

steps.name: Rosella
steps.text: Cecelia... You aren't done yet.

steps.name: Cecelia
steps.text: Right...

steps.name: Mostima
steps.text: Andoain, you've got a decent crowd here.

steps.name: Mostima
steps.text: You brought so many with you just to get Cecelia?

steps.name: Mostima
steps.text: Oh, almost forgot. I have a message for you. It's from the guy in the Lock and Key—

steps.name: Mostima
steps.text: Your bravery is commendable, but you won't like the final answer.

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: Thank you for that. I may not be fortunate enough to walk my path with it, but I benefited greatly from its opening my eyes all those years ago.

steps.name: Mostima
steps.text: Look at you... Are you sure you 'benefited?'

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: Only the wearer knows where the shoe pinches.

steps.name: Fiammetta
steps.text: —Not good! Ezell, stand back!

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: Ah...
Can you believe it—
I saw an ocean formed of faith.

steps.name: Fiammetta
steps.text: That concludes the report for this operation. Some of my colleagues present were involved in the incident. If you have anything to add, please do.

steps.name: Apostolic Knight
steps.text: Brothers and sisters, I propose we immediately declare a state of emergency across the entire city. Andoain is already enough trouble to deal with, but now we have a 'mixed-blood Sankta' on our hands too.

steps.name: Velliv
steps.text: Gun-Knight Giovanni, the conference is set to open soon. Surely you know that a state of emergency would lead to panic among the envoys?

steps.name: Apostolic Knight
steps.text: Your Eminence, we face a dangerous element. If a little panic could solve the problem at hand, I consider that an easy win.

steps.name: Velliv
steps.text: His Holiness has been planning this conference for years... the 'Summit of Nations.' It could be the key to Laterano's primacy on land as we know it, but now... a panic threatens to destroy this key.

steps.name: Apostolic Knight
steps.text: And how do you know that Andoain won't bring this conference to ruin if you leave him be?

steps.name: Oren
steps.text: No need to worry, Gun-Knight Giovanni. We're talking about a group of desperate people without a future and a small girl of unknown background.

steps.name: Apostolic Knight
steps.text: Oren, how do you think we Laterans have enjoyed peace for a millennium? It's because we stayed vigilant, taking no chances with such uncertainties!

steps.name: Oren
steps.text: (Even though Laterans set off explosions on the streets day in and day out, huh?)

steps.name: Oren
steps.text: The way I see it, the Reverend Gun-Knight just might be looking for an opportunity to use that awe-inspiring but so often holstered gun of yours?

steps.name: Apostolic Knight
steps.text: I take pride in my gun. Got a problem with that?!

steps.name: Fiammetta
steps.text: Please, this is urgent. May I continue?

steps.name: Apostolic Knight
steps.text: ...You may.

steps.name: Fiammetta
steps.text: I'm sure you all know that Mostima and I used to... work with Andoain.

steps.name: Fiammetta
steps.text: The Andoain I know isn't one to go off half-cocked. He wouldn't start a war without preparing for it. So even though he could sow chaos in Laterano, he wouldn't do it without a reason.

steps.name: Fiammetta
steps.text: The only clue the Astray have given us so far is their attempts on the mixed-blood girl called Cecelia.

steps.name: Fiammetta
steps.text: We can surmise that taking her is their primary objective.

steps.name: Fiammetta
steps.text: And since they already have her in their possession, I think Andoain's next step is very likely to be... exfiltrating Laterano.

steps.name: Fiammetta
steps.text: Therefore, I suggest we focus on the two following points.

steps.name: Fiammetta
steps.text: First, we need to step up our border controls and deploy more guards to the crossings. We should also form a special elite squad to locate their hideout and bring Andoain in.

steps.name: Fiammetta
steps.text: Secondly, to be on the safe side, I would like the Seventh Tribunal to lead the investigation into whether the Astray have made contact with the visiting envoys to determine whether or not they are targeting the conference.

steps.name: Fiammetta
steps.text: As for the conference itself...

steps.name: Mostima
steps.text: Proceed according to plan, right? That's what you have in mind, isn't it? We're just testing the waters, anyway.

steps.name: Mostima
steps.text: Oh, I've got to say, though. The cold buffet's desserts are disgusting. The cactus tarts are an atrocity. I would like to see some improvement there.

steps.name: The Pope
steps.text: I think there's a certain charm to the taste.

steps.name: Velliv
steps.text: I agree with Mostima on that point, and that point alone.

steps.name: Apostolic Knight
steps.text: Blasphemy! I think they're delicious!

steps.name: Oren
steps.text: Gun-Knight Giovanni has spoken. I suppose we can all agree, then?

steps.name: Velliv
steps.text: Agreed.

steps.name: Mostima
steps.text: Anything that Giovanni likes, you know is bound to be terrible.

steps.name: Apostolic Knight
steps.text: Mostima, belittling me again, are you?!

steps.name: The Pope
steps.text: Please, my children, quiet down. I'm too old for all this bickering.

steps.name: The Pope
steps.text: The laws instruct us to face the unknown with goodwill...

steps.name: The Pope
steps.text: We mustn't treat fruit tarts with such scorn.

steps.name: Velliv
steps.text: And why am I unfamiliar with this law?

steps.name: The Pope
steps.text: I just thought of it this morning.

steps.name: Fiammetta
steps.text: Your Holiness...

steps.name: The Pope
steps.text: We'll go with your plan.

steps.name: The Pope
steps.text: Vel, Giovanni, give Fiammetta all the help she needs.

steps.name: The Pope
steps.text: Andoain... will make his way to his goal.

steps.name: Mostima
steps.text: Phew... This is why I hate closed-door meetings...

steps.name: Fiammetta
steps.text: We spent three minutes on the main topic! The rest of the meeting was everyone babbling their stupid side conversations!

steps.name: Ezell
steps.text: Excuse me, Seniores? May I ask what the decision was?

steps.name: Fiammetta
steps.text: You're still here.

steps.name: Fiammetta
steps.text: I'm taking over the Andoain case. Thank you for your work the past couple days. You should head home to get some rest. I'll talk to the Notarial Hall later. Everything you've done will be written off as you helping us out.

steps.name: Ezell
steps.text: Miss Fiammetta, I...

steps.name: Fiammetta
steps.text: Anything that comes after this is way beyond the bounds of your authority and ability. Don't forget. You're still in training.

steps.name: Fiammetta
steps.text: I know you're worried about Cecelia, but I'm taking over this case, and that's the best case scenario you could hope for.

steps.name: Ezell
steps.text: Miss Fiammetta, are you friends with this... fallen angel? And the both of you are familiar with Andoain?

steps.name: Fiammetta
steps.text: That's right.

steps.name: Ezell
steps.text: Is that your answer to both of those questions?

steps.name: Fiammetta
steps.text: We aren't familiar. We're nemeses.

steps.name: Fiammetta
steps.text: But don't you worry. I won't take it out on Cecelia. I don't really understand what was going on with her this morning... but she's still a kid.

steps.name: Fiammetta
steps.text: What about you? You stayed there for two whole days. Did Andoain say anything to you?

steps.name: Ezell
steps.text: Just a bunch of heretical nonsense.

steps.name: Fiammetta
steps.text: I suggest you forget all of it, then.

steps.name: Fiammetta
steps.text: You still have your whole life ahead of you, right?

steps.name: Fiammetta
steps.text: Go home and take a couple days off, then keep up with your good work at the Notarial Hall. You are pretty qualified for the job if you ask me.

steps.name: Mostima
steps.text: Cherish your life, you know? Life in Laterano is precious. Even I look back on it fondly sometimes.

steps.name: Ezell
steps.text: My life...

steps.name: Ezell
steps.text: Right, unlike them, I'm just a regular nobody.

steps.name: Ezell
steps.text: Okay, let's clock out!

steps.name: Patia
steps.text: The Pontifica Cohors have taken over the border checkpoints, and the Apostolic Knights are keeping an eye out for us too. We won't be making it out anytime soon... We have a safehouse, but still...

steps.name: Patia
steps.text: I can't get in touch with Oren either... Dammit!

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: No matter. We can wait.

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: Cecelia?

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: Do you regret your decision?

steps.name: Cecelia
steps.text: I don't know...

steps.name: Cecelia
steps.text: But if I went with Miss Fiammetta... she would've taken me... to the Basilica, right?

steps.name: Cecelia
steps.text: I still haven't figured out... my goodbye to Mamma.

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: It's okay, Cecelia. You still have lots of time to think.

steps.name: Cecelia
steps.text: Mister Friar... There was a lady with horns and a halo in the Ecclesia Requietum just now... Is she... a Sankta?

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: Maybe. Maybe not. It's up to her to decide.

steps.name: Cecelia
steps.text: I thought... Sankta are Sankta?

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: That's true for most of us.

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: But some people get to choose. Or perhaps I should say they don't have a choice but to choose, because of some... unfortunate circumstance.

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: Incidentally, you too have to choose, Cecelia. As for whether that is fortunate or not... no one can tell.

steps.name: Cecelia
steps.text: Can't the Sankta be with the Sarkaz?

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: Of course they can. You are the living proof.

steps.name: Cecelia
steps.text: But... I'm causing everyone a lot of trouble, right?

steps.name: Cecelia
steps.text: Even Mister Ezell...

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: If you're always worrying about everything, you won't get anything done.

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: People will always fight. Neither 'gentleness' nor 'understanding' can stop that.

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: A lot of times, when people fight, it's not because one side is right and one side is wrong. It's because the things that both sides have to do conflict with each other.

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: In other words, the things that you and I need to do are different, and that means we're in somebody else's way.

steps.name: Cecelia
steps.text: Why can't we go the same way together?

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: Because, for a lot of people, the path that they take is determined by the path itself.

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: For example, the Sankta and the Sarkaz. No one can say why the two sides fought each other at first, but the hatred between them has paved the road for everyone.

steps.name: Cecelia
steps.text: Can't we choose our own path?

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: We can, Cecelia, but it's not that simple. If you want to leave the path you are on and find a new path forward, you must first make your way through a boundless wilderness...

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: It's vast and empty there. You might never find that new path, even if you give up everything you've ever known.

steps.name: Cecelia
steps.text: Then... why do we still have to look?

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: Right... why do we have to look?

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: Maybe it's because that's what we want.

steps.name: Cecelia
steps.text: 'What we want...' Is that so important?

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: It's the only thing we still have.

steps.name: Cecelia
steps.text: Mister Friar... Can I ask a question?

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: Go ahead.

steps.name: Cecelia
steps.text: What is it that you want?

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: Cecelia, can I tell you a little story?

steps.name: Cecelia
steps.text: Sure, Mister Friar. Go ahead.

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: Many years ago, when I was still young, I ran into some... setbacks, and then I left.

steps.name: Cecelia
steps.text: Where did you go?

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: Anywhere. I traveled everywhere.

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: There was a place I stayed for a while. It was a very small town, and it felt a little like my hometown.

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: But it was even more run-down. Life was tough for everyone there.

steps.name: Cecelia
steps.text: (Huh? That doesn't sound like Laterano...)

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: Once, I passed by the town's pub and came across a humming drunkard. He threw up all over me and insisted that I'd tripped him, and that I should pay for his drink.

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: Everyone in the pub... no, everyone in town laughed at him and cursed at him.

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: Those who were scared of him avoided him. Everyone called him a dirty, filthy moron, a lowlife, a sick scumbag... He was a Sarkaz.

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: They never chased him out of the town, however. He kept living from one day to the next, doing little odd jobs.

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: Then, on one windy, rainy night, a night when no one would go outside, the church's bell started to ring. It was an alarm, and it woke everyone up... There were... some bad people in town.

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: It was lucky that the bells woke everyone. It was hard, but we chased the bad people away. No one knew who rang the bells, and we all thought it was a miracle...

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: I headed in the direction of the bell tower and reached the wastes beyond. There, I found the church watchman digging a grave. Next to him was a cart, and in it a thin coffin, with the Sarkaz drunkard inside, wounded all over.

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: I started to help digging. The watchman kept complaining as he dug. He said he was saving the casket for his mother and it was a waste to give it to a Sarkaz. Then he complained that he'd have to bury the sick Sarkaz...

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: The watchman said that, not long after the bells started ringing, the Sarkaz came and knocked on his door, telling him to run, before the man died at his doorstep.

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: The watchman said that since he saw it was about to rain, he couldn't bear seeing the Sarkaz man sleep out in the streets, and so he let him into the bell tower for the night.

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: He kept complaining and kept digging. Then, when he was finished, he stood in front of the grave and sang a song that the drunkard always used to sing, even though he didn't remember how the second half went.

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: In the end, he complained a little more, and poured half a bottle on the grave.

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: The winds through hills on high...♪ Tail the hero's farflung stride...♪ Over long ways long...♪ Over briars and thorns...♪

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: Sorry, I don't remember it either.

steps.name: Cecelia
steps.text: That's... the song that Mamma and Rosella taught me...

steps.name: Cecelia
steps.text: So... the Sarkaz man rang the bell?

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: I think he did.

steps.name: Cecelia
steps.text: So he was the hero that saved everyone?

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: Maybe. I don't know if someone like him can be called a hero, but I think most people probably wouldn't want to call him one.

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: Maybe he was just trying to help the watchman who helped him.

steps.name: Cecelia
steps.text: What about you, Mister Friar? Do you think he was a hero?

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: What is a hero, Cecelia?

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: I thought about it for a long time... but I know that the answer to this question doesn't tell us who the Sarkaz man was. Rather, it tells us who I am.

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: I don't think he himself climbed up the bell tower to be a hero.

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: But it doesn't matter if we sing his praises, look at him with scorn, or even forget about him. None of that changes anything about him anymore.

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: All the questions that I pondered have nothing to do with him. Only me. Why did I witness this? What does it mean to me? How is it going to guide me forward?

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: It is always the living who are questioned.

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: But I kept thinking and thinking, what if he didn't do what he did?

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: What if he did it, but led the fanatics... the bad people to the bell tower?

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: What if the townspeople couldn't fend the bad people off even after they got woken up?

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: And what if... what if he even died on the bell tower, and no one ever found him?

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: There are no guaranteed successes, and there are no choices that are certain to be right.

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: So I came to this conclusion. On that rainy night, he climbed up the bell tower because he wanted to.

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: It's the most straightforward conclusion, out of somewhat stubborn goodwill.

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: Whether that's true or not doesn't concern him.

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: He was a hero, no different from the hero in the song.

steps.name: Rosella
steps.text: The winds through hills on high...♪ Tail the hero's farflung stride...♪

steps.name: Cecelia
steps.text: Over long ways long...♪ Over briars and thorns...♪
Everyone starts humming the song.
Their quiet singing drifts throughout the room.
I feel peace.
In this Lateran evening.
A peace that I have not known for a long time.

steps.name: Cecelia
steps.text: Are you thinking something, Mister Friar?

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: No, nothing at all.

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: Thank you, Cecelia.

steps.name: Cecelia
steps.text: You're looking at something...

steps.name: Cecelia
steps.text: Is that a bell tower?

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: It's Laterano's bell tower. A very, very old tower made of stone. I often went there when I still lived in Laterano. It was so close to Heaven.

steps.name: Cecelia
steps.text: Heaven... Is that where Mamma is?

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: If that's where you wish for her to be, that's where she is.

steps.name: Cecelia
steps.text: Mister Friar, could you help me with something?
